question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

When I bought the book, I thought it will be interesting.
options: thought
When
will
bought
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "will"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence uses past tense verbs like "bought" and "thought".
☛ Will is used for future tense, but here, "would" is correct as it reflects a past thought about the future.
☛ In reported past thoughts, we use would, not will.
☛ Correct Sentence: "I thought it would be interesting."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Sequence of Tenses: If the main verb is in the past tense, the subordinate clause must align (past/past perfect).
☛ Will vs. Would:
- Will → Future (present/future context).
- Would → Future-in-the-past (indirect speech/thoughts).
☛ Example:
- Incorrect: He told me he will help.
- Correct: He told me he would help. --------------

Explanation:

☛ will का प्रयोग future tense में होता है, लेकिन यहाँ past tense के संदर्भ में "would" का प्रयोग सही होगा।
☛ Reporting past thoughts (भूतकाल में सोचा गया) के लिए would का प्रयोग होता है, will नहीं।
☛ Correct Sentence: "I thought it would be interesting."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Sequence of Tenses: यदि मुख्य क्रिया (main verb) भूतकाल (past) में है, तो subordinate clause भी past या past perfect में होना चाहिए।
☛ Will vs. Would:
- Will → Future (वर्तमान या भविष्य के संदर्भ में)।
- Would → Past में future की बात (indirect speech/thoughts)।
☛ Example:
- Incorrect: She said she will come.
- Correct: She said she would come.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.


My teacher told me that / all that / glitters was not gold.
options: No error
My teacher told me that
all that
glitters was not gold
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "glitters was not gold"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the phrase "glitters was not gold" where "glitters" is in Present Tense while "was" is in Past Tense.
☛ The sentence means "My teacher told me that all that glitters is not gold", which expresses a universal truth requiring Present Tense.
☛ The correct phrase should be: "glitter is not gold" as it states a permanent truth.
☛ Using "was" is incorrect because it indicates Past Tense, whereas Present Tense is needed here.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Universal Truths or Habitual Actions are always expressed in Present Indefinite Tense.
☛ Past Tense is used only for actions that occurred in the past.
☛ Even if the Main Clause is in Past Tense, universal truths remain in Present Tense.

Example:
Incorrect - Our teacher told us that water boils at 100°C.
Correct - Our teacher told us that water boils at 100°C.
question_hi:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.


My teacher told me that / all that / glitters was not gold.
options_hi: No error
My teacher told me that
all that
glitters was not gold
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "glitters was not gold"

Explanation:
☛ दिए गए वाक्य में "glitters was not gold" में एक गलती है। यहाँ "glitters" एक वर्तमान काल (Present Tense) की क्रिया है, जबकि "was" भूतकाल (Past Tense) की क्रिया है।
☛ वाक्य का अर्थ है "मेरे शिक्षक ने मुझे बताया कि जो चमकता है वह सोना नहीं होता"। यह एक सामान्य सत्य (universal truth) को दर्शाता है, जिसमें वर्तमान काल का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
☛ सही वाक्यांश होना चाहिए: "glitter is not gold" क्योंकि यह एक स्थायी सत्य को व्यक्त करता है।
☛ "was" का प्रयोग गलत है क्योंकि यह भूतकाल को दर्शाता है, जबकि यहाँ वर्तमान काल की आवश्यकता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ सामान्य सत्य (Universal Truth) या आदतन क्रिया (Habitual Action) को हमेशा Present Indefinite Tense में व्यक्त किया जाता है।
☛ भूतकाल (Past Tense) का प्रयोग केवल उन घटनाओं के लिए होता है जो अतीत में घटित हुई हों।
☛ यदि मुख्य वाक्य (Main Clause) भूतकाल में है, तो भी सामान्य सत्य को वर्तमान काल में ही रखा जाता है।

Example:
Incorrect - The teacher said that Earth revolves around the Sun.
Correct - The teacher said that Earth revolves around the Sun.

question: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I love the taste of fresh strawberries in the summer.
He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
She is the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine."

Explanation:
☛ The given sentence has an article error. "He is chef" should be "He is a chef" because we use the indefinite article ('a') when referring to someone's profession for the first time.
☛ Articles (a, an, the) are used before nouns. Here, 'chef' is a countable noun, and since it’s being mentioned generically, the article 'a' is necessary.
☛ The relative clause ("who specialises in Italian cuisine") is correct, but the missing article makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Indefinite Articles (a/an): Used when introducing a person/thing for the first time or in a general sense. Example: She is a doctor.
☛ Definite Article (the): Used for specific nouns already known to the listener. Example: She is the winner of the Nobel Prize.
☛ Zero Article: No article is used with proper nouns or uncountable nouns. Example: I love fresh strawberries.

Example:
Incorrect - He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
Correct - He is a chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
question_hi: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options_hi: I love the taste of fresh strawberries in the summer.
He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
She is the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine."

Explanation:
☛ दिए गए वाक्य में article का गलत प्रयोग हुआ है। "He is chef" के बजाय "He is a chef" होना चाहिए क्योंकि यहाँ indefinite article ('a') का प्रयोग होता है जब हम किसी व्यक्ति के पेशे के बारे में बात करते हैं।
☛ Articles (a, an, the) का प्रयोग nouns से पहले होता है। यहाँ 'chef' एक countable noun है और पहली बार बात कर रहे हैं, इसलिए 'a' का प्रयोग जरूरी है।
☛ इस वाक्य में relative clause ("who specialises in Italian cuisine") सही है, लेकिन article की गलती से पूरा वाक्य गलत हो जाता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Indefinite Articles (a/an): जब हम किसी व्यक्ति या वस्तु के बारे में पहली बार बात करते हैं या उसे generalize करते हैं, तो 'a/an' का प्रयोग करते हैं। Example: She is a doctor.
☛ Definite Article (the): जब हम किसी specific व्यक्ति या वस्तु की बात करते हैं, तो 'the' का प्रयोग करते हैं। Example: She is the winner of the Nobel Prize.
☛ Zero Article: कुछ nouns (जैसे proper nouns, uncountable nouns) के पहले article नहीं लगता। Example: I love fresh strawberries.

Example:
Incorrect - He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
Correct - He is a chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

Sohan is the older brother of my best friend.
options: good
elder
to my
an
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "elder"

Explanation:
☛ 'Older' should be replaced with 'elder' because it refers to seniority between two brothers in a family.
☛ 'Elder' is used specifically for comparing family members (e.g., siblings), whereas 'older' is used for general comparisons.
☛ Since the sentence mentions "brother" (a family relation), 'elder' is the correct choice.
☛ Note: 'Elder' is never followed by 'than', but 'older' can be used with 'than' (Rahul is older than Rohan).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Adjectives: Both 'elder' and 'older' are comparative forms, but their usage differs.
☛ 'Elder' is used only for people (especially family) and comes before a noun (e.g., elder son).
☛ 'Older' can compare people, objects, or places (e.g., This car is older than mine).

Example:
Incorrect - He is the older member of the team.
Correct - He is the elder member of the team.

☛ 'Elder' का प्रयोग परिवार के सदस्यों की तुलना (जैसे भाई-बहन) में किया जाता है, जबकि 'older' हर प्रकार की तुलना में इस्तेमाल होता है।
☛ वाक्य में "brother" (परिवार संबंध) होने के कारण 'elder' सही विकल्प है।
☛ ध्यान दें: 'Elder' के बाद 'than' नहीं आता, जबकि 'older' के बाद 'than' का प्रयोग हो सकता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Adjectives: 'Elder' और 'older' दोनों comparative degree के शब्द हैं, लेकिन इनका प्रयोग अलग-अलग संदर्भों में होता है।
☛ 'Elder' केवल व्यक्तियों (खासकर परिवार) के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है और यह noun से पहले आता है (जैसे—elder brother)।

Example:
Incorrect - She is the older sister in the family.
Correct - She is the elder sister in the family.

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

This car is lesser expensive than the one I had come to buy.
options: came
ones
for
less
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "less"

Explanation:
☛ Error: The word "lesser" is incorrect in this sentence as it is the wrong form of the comparative adjective.
☛ Correct Usage: "Less" is used with uncountable nouns (e.g., money, time) in the comparative degree, while "fewer" is used with countable nouns.
☛ Sentence Structure: Here, "expensive" (cost) is an uncountable concept, so "less" is the correct choice.
☛ Key Point: "Lesser" is generally used in the context of quality or importance, not quantity or degree.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Adjectives: Both "less" and "fewer" are comparative adjectives, but they are used in different contexts.
☛ Uncountable Nouns: "Less" is used with uncountable nouns (e.g., water, sugar).
☛ Countable Nouns: "Fewer" is used with countable nouns (e.g., books, cars).
☛ Example:
Incorrect - She has lesser money than her brother.
Correct - She has less money than her brother.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error and select the option which rectifies that error.


The SNAP-10 A / was launched on 3 April 1965 / on a Atlas-Agena D rocket / from Vandenberg Air Force Base.
options: at Vandenberg Air Force Base.
was launch on 3 April 1965
A SNAP-10 A
on an Atlas-Agena D rocket
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "on an Atlas-Agena D rocket"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "on a Atlas-Agena D rocket" is incorrect because "Atlas-Agena D" starts with a vowel sound (A).
☛ According to English grammar rules, "an" must be used before words starting with vowel sounds (A, E, I, O, U), not "a".
☛ Here, "an" is correct before "Atlas-Agena D" as it begins with "A".
☛ Other options like "was launch" (incorrect verb form), "A SNAP-10 A" (redundant article), and "at Vandenberg Air Force Base." (unnecessary full stop) are incorrect.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Indefinite Articles (a/an):
- Use "a" before words starting with consonant sounds (e.g., a dog).
- Use "an" before words starting with vowel sounds (e.g., an egg).
☛ Note: It depends on the sound, not spelling. For example, an hour (silent "h").

Example:
Incorrect - She is a European.
Correct - She is a European. (Exception: "European" starts with a "Y" sound, treated as a consonant.)

☛ अंग्रेजी व्याकरण के नियमानुसार, जब कोई शब्द स्वर से शुरू होता है, तो "a" के बजाय "an" का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛ यहाँ "Atlas-Agena D" के पहले "an" का प्रयोग सही है क्योंकि यह "A" से शुरू होता है।
☛ अन्य विकल्प जैसे "was launch" (गलत क्रिया रूप), "A SNAP-10 A" (अनावश्यक आर्टिकल), और "at Vandenberg Air Force Base." (अनावश्यक पूर्णविराम) गलत हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Indefinite Articles (a/an):

Incorrect - He is a honest man.
Correct - He is an honest man.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The little child / wrote his name / quick / on the wall.
options: The little child
quick
on the wall
wrote his name
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "quick"

Explanation:
☛ The word "quick" is incorrectly used in the sentence. An Adverb is required here to modify the verb "wrote".
☛ "Quick" is an Adjective that describes nouns/pronouns, whereas "quickly" is an Adverb describing verbs.
☛ The correct sentence should use "quickly" to indicate how the child wrote (the manner of writing).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjective vs Adverb: Adjectives (e.g., quick, happy) describe nouns/pronouns, while Adverbs (e.g., quickly, happily) modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
☛ Adverb Formation: Many adverbs are formed by adding "ly" to adjectives (quick → quickly, happy → happily).
☛ Exam Tip: In error spotting, check words following verbs—if they describe the action, they must be adverbs.

Example:
Incorrect - He speaks loud.
Correct - He speaks loudly.

The little child / wrote his name / quick / on the wall.
options_hi: The little child
quick

wrote his name
solution_hi:

Explanation:
☛ वाक्य में "quick" शब्द का प्रयोग गलत तरीके से किया गया है। यहाँ Adverb की आवश्यकता है क्योंकि यह verb "wrote" को modify कर रहा है।
☛ "Quick" एक Adjective है जो noun या pronoun को describe करता है, जबकि "quickly" एक Adverb है जो verb को describe करता है।
☛ सही वाक्य में "quickly" का प्रयोग होना चाहिए ताकि यह बताया जा सके कि बच्चे ने कैसे लिखा (how the child wrote)।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjective vs Adverb: Adjective (जैसे quick, happy) nouns/pronouns की विशेषता बताते हैं, जबकि Adverbs (जैसे quickly, happily) verbs, adjectives या दूसरे adverbs को modify करते हैं।
☛ Adverb Formation: अक्सर "ly" जोड़कर Adjective से Adverb बनाया जाता है, जैसे quick → quickly, happy → happily।
☛ Exam Tip: Error spotting में verb के बाद आए शब्द पर ध्यान दें—यदि वह verb की गति/स्थिति बता रहा है, तो Adverb होना चाहिए।

Example:
Incorrect - She runs quick.
Correct - She runs quickly.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) It is said / (B) that fortune / (C) favour the / (D) brave.
options: D
A
C
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "C"

Explanation:
☛ Part (C) contains the error due to Subject-Verb Agreement rule violation.
☛ "Fortune" is a Singular Noun, hence it requires a Singular Verb (favours).
☛ "Favour" is a Plural Verb, making it Grammatically Incorrect.
☛ Correct Sentence: "Fortune favours the brave." (Literal Meaning: Luck supports the courageous.)

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular Subjects take Singular Verbs, Plural Subjects take Plural Verbs.
☛ Third-Person Singular Rule: Verbs with He/She/It or Singular Nouns in Present Indefinite Tense end with 's'/'es'.
☛ Collective Nouns: Treat words like "team," "jury" as singular unless individual members are emphasized.

Example:
Incorrect - The committee are divided.
Correct - The committee is divided.

The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) It is said / (B) that fortune / (C) favour the / (D) brave.
options_hi: D
A
C
B
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "C"

Explanation:
☛ भाग (C) में त्रुटि है क्योंकि यहां Subject-Verb Agreement का नियम लागू होता है।
☛ "fortune" एक Singular Noun है, इसलिए इसके साथ Singular Verb (favours) का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
☛ "favour" Plural Verb है जो Grammatically Incorrect है।
☛ वाक्य का सही रूप होगा: "fortune favours the brave" (किस्मत बहादुरों का साथ देती है)।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular Subject के साथ Singular Verb और Plural Subject के साथ Plural Verb आती है।
☛ Third-Person Singular Rule: He/She/It या Singular Nouns के साथ Present Indefinite Tense में Verb में 's' या 'es' लगता है।
☛ Common Errors: Collective Nouns (जैसे team, family) को Singular मानकर Singular Verb का प्रयोग करें।

Example:
Incorrect - The team are playing well.
Correct - The team is playing well.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

options: is
a

beautiful colour
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "The blue"

Explanation:
☛ The blue is incorrect because the definite article 'The' is wrongly used here.
☛ Names of colours do not take 'The' unless referring to a specific group (e.g., "The blue team").
☛ The correct sentence should be: "Blue is a beautiful colour.", where 'Blue' (adjective/noun) is used without any article.
☛ As per general rules, avoid 'The' with colour names (red, blue) unless denoting a specific category.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Articles are used with countable nouns (e.g., a pen, the tree) or unique things (e.g., the moon).
☛ Abstract nouns (e.g., happiness) or general terms (e.g., colours, music) usually take no article.
☛ Exception: Phrases like "The elderly" use 'The' + Adjective to represent a group.

Example:
Incorrect - The patience is a virtue.
Correct - Patience is a virtue.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.


Tuntun and her friends dance beautiful.
options: dance
Tuntun
beautiful
and her friends
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "beautiful"

Explanation:
☛ The word "beautiful" is incorrect in the given sentence because it is an adjective, whereas an adverb is required here.
☛ In "Tuntun and her friends dance beautiful.", "dance" is a verb, and to describe how the action is performed, an adverb ("beautifully") should be used.
☛ Adjectives (e.g., beautiful) modify nouns or pronouns, while adverbs (e.g., beautifully) modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
☛ Exams often test adjective/adverb confusion, so understanding these rules is crucial.

Grammar Rules:
☛ To form an adverb, we typically add "-ly" to the adjective (e.g., quick → quickly, happy → happily).
☛ Some adverbs (e.g., fast, hard) have the same form as adjectives but change meaning based on context.
☛ Linking verbs (e.g., seem, appear, feel) are followed by adjectives, while action verbs require adverbs.

Example:
Incorrect - He runs quick.
Correct - He runs quickly.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adverb बनाने के लिए अक्सर adjective के अंत में "-ly" जोड़ा जाता है (उदाहरण: quick → quickly, happy → happily)।

Example:

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

You shall repented tomorrow for your misdeeds.
options: tomorrow
for your misdeeds
You
shall repented
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "shall repented"

Explanation:
☛ The error in the sentence lies in "shall repented" because "shall" is a modal verb that must be followed by the base form of the verb (V1), but here the past participle form (V3) "repented" is used.
☛ The correct structure should be: "shall + repent" (V1) as modal verbs (shall, will, can, may, etc.) always take the base verb.
☛ "Tomorrow" and "for your misdeeds" are correct as they indicate time and reason respectively.
☛ "You" is also correct as it is the subject pronoun fitting the sentence structure.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Modal Verbs (shall, will, can, may, must, etc.) are always followed by the base form of the verb (V1).
☛ Past participle (V3) is used in perfect tenses or passive voice, not with modal verbs.
☛ In future tense, "shall/will + V1" is used.

Example:
Incorrect - She will eaten the cake.
Correct - She will eat the cake.

Grammar Rules:

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

I have seen / a movie / on schooling / yesterday.
options: a movie
yesterday
on schooling
I have seen
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "I have seen"

Explanation:
☛ The segment 'I have seen' is incorrect because the adverb 'yesterday' (past time marker) requires the use of Simple Past Tense, not Present Perfect Tense.
☛ Present Perfect Tense is used when the time of action is unspecified or connected to the present.
☛ Simple Past Tense should be used here since the action occurred at a specific past time (yesterday).
☛ Correct sentence: "I saw a movie on schooling yesterday."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Present Perfect Tense: Has/Have + V3 → Used for unspecified time or present relevance.
☛ Simple Past Tense: V2 → Used for definite past time (e.g., yesterday, last year).
☛ Past Perfect Tense: Had + V3 → Used for the earlier action in two past actions.

Example:
Incorrect - She has completed her work yesterday.
Correct - She completed her work yesterday.

Grammar Rules:

☛ Past Perfect Tense: Had + V3 → दो क्रियाओं में जो पहले हुई हो, उसे दिखाने के लिए।

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


A music / is a great way / to express / your emotions.
options: to express
A music
your emotions
is a great way
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "A music"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the segment "A music" because "music" is an uncountable noun.
☛ We do not use indefinite articles ("a" or "an") with uncountable nouns.
☛ The word "music" itself is sufficient and does not require any article before it.
☛ The correct phrase should be simply "Music" or "Some music" if quantity needs to be indicated.
☛ This mistake is frequently tested in competitive exams as it tests basic rules of articles and countable/uncountable nouns.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Uncountable nouns like milk, water, music, advice etc. do not take "a/an".
☛ They cannot be made plural (e.g., "musics" is incorrect).
☛ To show quantity, use "some", "a piece of" etc. (some music, a piece of advice).
☛ If a word can be both countable and uncountable (e.g., "light"), context must be checked.

Example:
Incorrect - A music is playing.
Correct - Music is playing. or Some music is playing.

question:

options: This is the most old standing structure of Chola architecture in India.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India."

Explanation:
☛ Eldest is used only for people, while Oldest is used for objects, buildings, or places.
☛ Here, the sentence refers to a structure of Chola architecture, so "oldest" is the correct term.
☛ In Superlative Degree, the correct form of "old" is "oldest", not "eldest".
☛ Standing structure is an inanimate object, hence "eldest" is incorrect.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Eldest vs Oldest: "Eldest" is used only for family members (e.g., siblings). Example: She is the eldest in her family.
☛ Oldest is used for objects, buildings, or historical places. Example: This is the oldest temple in the city.
☛ Superlative Degree: For single-syllable adjectives (e.g., old, tall), add "-est" to form the superlative.

Example:
Incorrect - This is the eldest building in the town.
Correct - This is the oldest building in the town.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Radha will have learnt cooking by the time she will have married.
options: learnt cooking
she will have married
Radha will have
by the time
solution:
Solution:** Correct Answer is **"she will have married"**

**Explanation:**
☛ The sentence uses **Future Perfect Tense** to indicate an action completed by a certain future time. However, **"she will have married"** is incorrect in this context because **"married"** signifies a permanent state, making **Simple Future Tense (she gets married)** or **Future Perfect Continuous (she has been married)** more suitable.

☛ **Future Perfect Tense** is used when we talk about an action that will be completed before a specific time in the future.
☛ **"Married"** is a state that does not change over time, so using Perfect Tense becomes redundant.

**Grammar Rules:**
☛ **Future Perfect Tense** structure: **Subject + will/shall + have + V3 (Past Participle)**
☛ **Simple Future Tense** structure: **Subject + will/shall + V1 (Base Verb)**
☛ **Future Perfect Continuous Tense** structure: **Subject + will have been + V1 + ing**

**Example:**
Incorrect - *By next year, they will have lived here.*
Correct - *By next year, they will have been living here for a decade.* --

हल:** सही उत्तर है **"she will have married"**

☛ यहाँ **Future Perfect Tense** का प्रयोग होना चाहिए क्योंकि हम एक ऐसी घटना के बारे में बात कर रहे हैं जो भविष्य में किसी निश्चित समय तक पूरी हो चुकी होगी। परन्तु, **"she will have married"** इस संदर्भ में गलत है क्योंकि **"married"** एक स्थायी स्थिति है, इसलिए **Simple Future Tense (she gets married)** या **Future Perfect Continuous (she has been married)** का प्रयोग अधिक उपयुक्त होता।

☛ **Future Perfect Tense** का उपयोग वहाँ किया जाता है जहाँ किसी कार्य के भविष्य में किसी निश्चित समय तक पूरा होने की बात की जाती है।
☛ **"Married"** एक ऐसी स्थिति है जो समय के साथ परिवर्तित नहीं होती, इसीलिए **Perfect Tense** का प्रयोग अनावश्यक हो जाता है।

**Grammar Rules:**
☛ **Future Perfect Tense** संरचना: **Subject + will/shall + have + V3 (Past Participle)**
☛ **Simple Future Tense** संरचना: **Subject + will/shall + V1 (Base Verb)**
☛ **Future Perfect Continuous Tense** संरचना: **Subject + will have been + V1 + ing**

**Example:**
Incorrect - *By 2025, he will have gone to Delhi.*
Correct - *By 2025, he will have gone to Delhi twice.*

question:

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "B"

Explanation:
☛ Part (B) "Francis plays for" contains an error in Subject-Verb Agreement.
☛ The subject "Taylor, Richard, and Francis" is plural, so the verb must also be plural ("play"), not singular ("plays").
☛ Golden Rule: When two or more subjects are joined by "and," the verb is always plural.
☛ Example: "Peanut butter and jelly are my favorites." (Correct), "Peanut butter and jelly is my favorite." (Incorrect).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: The verb must match the subject in number (singular/plural).
☛ Compound Subjects: Subjects joined by "and" are treated as plural.
☛ Common Pitfalls: Collective nouns (e.g., team, committee) take singular verbs when acting as a unit but plural when referring to individual members.
Example: "The committee has decided." (Unit), "The committee have disagreed." (Members).

Example:
Incorrect - "Bread and butter is my breakfast." (If separate items)
Correct - "Bread and butter are my breakfast."

Example: "The team is playing." (Unit), "The team are arguing." (Individual members).

question:

☛ Platinum is a metal name (like gold, silver), and such nouns omit the unless referring to a specific instance (e.g., The platinum in this device is expensive.).
☛ Correct sentence: Platinum is a precious metal. (without the).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Uncountable nouns (e.g., water, advice) do not take indefinite articles (a/an).
☛ Use the only when the noun is specific (e.g., The advice you gave was helpful.).
☛ Metal names (gold, platinum) are typically used without articles in general contexts.

Example:
Incorrect - The silver is ductile.
Correct - Silver is ductile.

Solution: Correct Answer is "lately"

Explanation:

☛ For past actions, 'late' (after the usual time) is correct, not 'lately'.
☛ Correct Structure: "I had a bad habit of waking up late."

Grammar Rules:

- Late = After the expected time (works in all tenses), e.g., He arrived late yesterday.
☛ Past Perfect Tense ('had + V3') describes completed past habits/actions.

Example:
Incorrect - I had a meeting lately.
Correct - I had a meeting late.

question:

Mr Sharma would have left / the station / by this time / tomorrow.
options: Mr Sharma would have left
the station
by this time
tomorrow
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "Mr Sharma would have left"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "would have left" as it expresses a hypothetical past action (3rd conditional), while the sentence refers to a future time ("tomorrow").
☛ The correct phrase should be "will have left" (future perfect tense), used for actions completed before a specific future time.
☛ Future perfect structure: Subject + will/shall + have + past participle (V3).
☛ "By + time phrase" (e.g., by this time tomorrow) always pairs with future perfect tense.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Future Perfect Tense: Indicates completion of an action before a specified future time.
☛ Key markers: "by tomorrow/by 5 PM" or "by the time + clause".
☛ "Would have + V3" is strictly for unreal past conditions (e.g., If he had hurried, he would have caught the train).

Example:
Incorrect - They would have reached Delhi by next Monday.
Correct - They will have reached Delhi by next Monday.

☛ "By + time phrase" (by this time tomorrow) के साथ future perfect tense ही प्रयुक्त होता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Future Perfect Tense: यह टेंस भविष्य में किसी निश्चित समय तक पूर्ण हो चुके कार्य को दर्शाता है।

question:

for
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "shall be playing"

Explanation:
☛ The given sentence "I shall be playing for four hours." is grammatically correct.
☛ shall be playing is a correct future continuous tense form, indicating an action that will continue for a specified duration (four hours) in the future.
☛ I is the correct subject pronoun.

☛ For is used with durations, while since is used with specific time points.

Example:
Incorrect - I shall playing for four hours.
Correct - I shall be playing for four hours.

question:

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "B"

Explanation:

☛ Mathematical facts are always expressed in the Simple Present Tense, not continuous forms.
☛ The verb "coming" is inappropriate here as it implies an ongoing action, whereas mathematical results are permanent truths.
☛ The correct phrase should be: "two is" or "two equals".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Simple Present Tense is used for universal truths, habits, and routine actions.
☛ Present Continuous Tense is used only for actions happening now or temporary situations.
☛ Mathematical operations and results must always be in Simple Present since they are timeless facts.

Example:
Incorrect - Two is coming out to be four.
Correct - Two multiplied by two is four.

question:

options: I have

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "less books"

Explanation:
☛ Less is used with uncountable nouns (things that cannot be counted), such as water, sugar, money.
☛ Fewer is used with countable nouns (things that can be counted), such as books, pens, apples.
☛ Here, books is a countable noun, so fewer is correct, not less.
☛ The use of than is correct as it shows comparison.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Countable vs Uncountable Nouns: Countable nouns can be counted (e.g., chairs, dogs), while uncountable nouns cannot (e.g., milk, happiness).
☛ Less vs Fewer: Less is used with uncountable nouns, and fewer with countable nouns.
☛ Comparative Structures: Than is used after comparative adjectives (e.g., fewer, more, taller).

Example:
Incorrect - They have less books than I have.
Correct - They have fewer books than I have.

question:

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "gone out"

Explanation:

☛ The correct form should be "when the power went out" since "went out" (simple past) shows a sudden interruption.
☛ Gone out is a past participle and cannot be used without an auxiliary verb like "had".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Past Continuous + Simple Past: When a longer action (past continuous) is interrupted by a shorter action (simple past), the interrupting action takes simple past.
☛ Past Perfect Usage: If "gone out" were to be used, the sentence should include "had" as an auxiliary verb, e.g., "the power had gone out".

Example:
Incorrect - She was singing when the phone ringed.
Correct - She was singing when the phone rang. (Simple Past is correct)

☛ Correct preposition usage is crucial for sentence meaning.
☛ Verbs like translate, convert, change mandate into, not in.
☛ in vs. into: in denotes static position, whereas into implies motion/transformation.
☛ Exams frequently test prepositional errors, especially with verbs involving change.

Example:
Incorrect - The poem was translated in French.
Correct - The poem was translated into French.
question_hi:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


This scripture / has been /translated in / seventy languages.
options_hi: This scripture
seventy languages
translated in
has been
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "translated in"

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ translated in गलत है क्योंकि translate क्रिया के साथ into preposition का प्रयोग होता है, in का नहीं।
☛ Translate into का अर्थ है "किसी भाषा में अनुवाद करना"।
☛ in का प्रयोग स्थान, समय या स्थिति को दर्शाने के लिए होता है, जबकि into परिवर्तन या दिशा को दर्शाता है।
☛ इस वाक्य का सही रूप होगा: "This scripture has been translated into seventy languages."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Preposition का सही चुनाव वाक्य के अर्थ को प्रभावित करता है।
☛ Translate जैसी क्रियाओं के साथ into का प्रयोग अनिवार्य होता है।
☛ in vs. into: in स्थिर स्थिति दर्शाता है, जबकि into गति या परिवर्तन दर्शाता है।
☛ परीक्षा में prepositional errors अक्सर पूछे जाते हैं, विशेषकर translate, convert, change जैसी क्रियाओं के साथ।

Example:
Incorrect - The book was translated in Spanish.
Correct - The book was translated into Spanish.
